theme: Conditional minimum functions, renewal inference and practical knowledge
question: What minimum functional conditions does a complex society need over a stated horizon, and how can longevity and renewal traces make those conditions archaeologically testable?
outcome: A manuscript, conditional theory and 15-claim evidence map join independent delivered-output bounds, actual renewal operations, joint work windows and historically available enactment. Shared repair and learning develops a concrete alternative to separately costly training. The framework explains why urban form, residents and practical knowledge can have different persistence outcomes; a particular Harappan-to-textual contribution remains a separate historical test.
challenge: An unrestricted minimum list can misidentify political institutions or assume local closure. Separate cost sums can double-count shared operations. Preserving current work and source scope matters in a shared research workspace.
remedy: Define outcome, boundary, horizon and distribution before necessity claims; include carried inventory, substitution, imports, co-production and action information. Commission independent mathematical, source and manuscript review. Preserve 12 selected starting-byte snapshots and a 16,316-file start inventory, append navigation over current bytes, and retain earlier endpoints and local-only source witnesses.
retry_when: A predeclared service sequence or common sampling frame supplies independent demand/supply bounds, dated replacement operations and participation evidence. Extend with a new dated empirical study and include short-lived, interrupted and uncertain cases.
